25 What is the order of magnitude of the wavelengths of microwaves and X-rays?

hints: Look at the two columns in the table: one asks for wavelength of microwaves in $\text{m}$ and the other for wavelength of X-rays in $\text{m}$ as powers of 10.
Recall the order of the electromagnetic spectrum from long wavelength to short wavelength: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.
Compare the choices $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ and $10^{-6} \text{ m}$ for a centimetre-scale microwave oven wave, and $10^{3} \text{ m}$ and $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ for an atomic-scale X-ray wave.
walkthrough: Recall the electromagnetic spectrum in order of decreasing wavelength: radio waves have the longest wavelengths, then microwaves, then infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, then gamma rays with the shortest.

Microwaves lie just shorter than radio waves and longer than infrared. Their typical wavelength is centimetres, so the order of magnitude is $10^{-2} \text{ m}$, not $10^{-6} \text{ m}$ which is infrared.

X-rays lie between ultraviolet and gamma rays. Their typical wavelength is comparable to atomic spacing, about $0.1 \text{ nm}$, so the order of magnitude is $10^{-10} \text{ m}$, not $10^{3} \text{ m}$ which is a long radio wave.
Check the table: only the row with $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ for microwaves and $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ for X-rays gives both correct orders of magnitude.

A.explanation: Both values are wrong. $10^{-6} \text{ m}$ is typical of infrared, not microwaves, and $10^{3} \text{ m}$ is typical of radio waves, not X-rays.

B.explanation: The microwave value $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ is correct, but $10^{3} \text{ m}$ is far too large for X-rays and belongs to the radio region.

C.explanation: The X-ray value $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ is correct, but $10^{-6} \text{ m}$ is too short for microwaves and belongs to the infrared region.

D.explanation: Microwaves are of order $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ and X-rays are of order $10^{-10} \text{ m}$, matching the correct positions in the electromagnetic spectrum.
